title: 4.9.12.2. Mismatch between cell header algorithm, TD HEADERs, and platform accessibility APIs
body:
The algorithm in "4.9.12.2. Forming relationships between data cells and header cells" assumes a single header list for cells (as did HTML 4)

Modern accessibility APIs expose a pair of properties for cell headers: RowHeaders and ColumnHeaders (or similar): 

IAccessible2 (Firefox and Linux)
IAccessibleTableCell::columnHeaderCells
IAccessibleTableCell::rowHeaderCells
 
UIA (Windows)
ITableItemProvider::GetColumnHeaderItems
ITableItemProvider::GetRowHeaderItems 

NSAccessibility (Mac/iOS)
AccessibilityTableCell::columnHeaders
AccessibilityTableCell::rowHeaders

This allows screen readers to voice column headers when moving along a row, voice row headers when moving up or down a column, and provide separate commands to announce row or column header.  This also surfaces in ARIA as the columnheader and rowheader roles

This presents a problem for browser implementors trying to match up the single header list specified by the algorithm and the RowHeaders and ColumnHeaders lists exposed by accessibility APIs.

The biggest problem seems to be the TD HEADERS attribute since there's no way to specify whether the attribute references a row header or column header (NVDA has some clever heuristics, Safari just assumes they're column headers)

All of this lead to interop issues between different browsers / ATs.

This post has a lot of detail on current browser / AT behaviour along with links to underlying browser / AT source code:
http://www.powermapper.com/blog/table-headers-and-scope/

PS This issue was originally posted as a W3 HTML5  issue - which contains potentially useful comments:
https://github.com/w3c/html/issues/583#issuecomment-351223284
